Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]] and [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]; no use of the full Axiom of Choice is made here. Let $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, its normalized measure, the componentwise real Sobolev spaces $H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, and their weak-derivative and Fourier-coefficient conventions be exactly those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]]. In particular, $H^s$ is defined for integer $s\ge0$, the weak-derivative norm is equivalent to the Fourier-weight norm by [[lem-gr-periodic-fourier-differentiation-and-norm-equivalence]], and the trigonometric characters are a complete orthonormal system by [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]. A field is a function with the domain and codomain declaration of [[def-function]]; Sobolev fields are its $L^2$-equivalence classes, not pointwise representatives.

For finite $m\ge1$, open $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, compact $K\subseteq O$, $R\ge0$, and integer $s\ge5$, define the bounded admissible initial-state class

$$\mathcal S_s(K,R):=\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ has its continuous representative valued in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\}.$$

The representative is unique because two continuous functions equal almost everywhere on the torus agree everywhere. For a smooth periodic first-order reduction of the electrovacuum equations, its finite list of real component fields is identified with one such $\mathbb R^m$-valued function. The high-regularity initial metric and electromagnetic data are $h\in H^{s+1}$, $K,e,b\in H^s$, with $h$ uniformly positive definite; the product state and its first spatial metric derivatives lie in $H^s$. This is a definition of admissible function-space classes only; it asserts no existence result for a coupled Einstein-Maxwell reduction.

For physical units, one may introduce fixed scales $L_0>0$ in metres and $F_0>0$ in tesla, use dimensionless torus coordinates $y^i=x^i/L_0$, and replace each first metric derivative $v$ by $L_0v$ and each electromagnetic component $e,b$ by $e/F_0,b/F_0$. These constant invertible rescalings define the same finite-component Sobolev topology; they are bookkeeping conventions, not extra equations.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $m\ge1$, an open set
$O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ with the subspace topology and a nondegenerate open
interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$. All functions on
$\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ are those of [[def-gr-periodic-torus-and-sobolev-spaces]],
and smoothness on $I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$ means smoothness of the
representative in the sense of clause (e) of that item.

**(a) Coefficients.** A **periodic symmetric hyperbolic coefficient family** on
$O$ consists of smooth maps
$$A^\mu:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)\quad(\mu=0,1,2,3),\qquad B:I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O\to\mathbb R^m,$$
such that $A^0(t,x,u)$ is positive definite for every
$(t,x,u)\in I\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\times O$; here
$\operatorname{Sym}_m(\mathbb R)$ is the real vector space of symmetric
$m\times m$ matrices, identified with symmetric endomorphisms of $\mathbb R^m$
through the standard coordinate inner product, and positive definiteness means
$z^TA^0(t,x,u)z>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbb R^m$
([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

**(b) The system.** The associated **symmetric hyperbolic system** is
$$A^0(t,x,u)\,\partial_tu+\sum_{i=1}^3A^i(t,x,u)\,\partial_iu+B(t,x,u)=0 .\qquad(\star)$$

**(c) Values and norms.** For each integer $s\ge0$, an $H^s$ class
$u\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ **takes values in a set
$E\subseteq\mathbb R^m$** when it has a continuous representative whose values
lie in $E$. Such a representative is unique, since continuous functions equal
almost everywhere on the torus agree everywhere. A map $u:J\to H^s$ with
$J\subseteq I$ takes values in $E$ when every class $u(t)$ does. For compact
$K\subseteq O$ and $R\ge0$ put
$$\mathcal S_s(K,R):=\bigl\{u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m):u_0\text{ takes values in }K,\ \|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R\bigr\}.$$
When an item fixes $s$, it may abbreviate this class by $\mathcal S(K,R)$.

**(d) Classical solutions.** Let $s\ge2$ be an integer and let $J\subseteq I$ be
an interval. A **classical solution of $(\star)$ on
$J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$** is a $C^1$ map
$u:J\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}\to\mathbb R^m$ with $u(t,x)\in O$ for all
$(t,x)$ and $(\star)$ satisfied at every point, such that
$u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)$ and $\partial_tu\in L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$.

**(e) Sobolev solutions.** Let $s\ge5$ be an integer and let $J\subseteq I$ be
an open interval. A map
$u:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ is a **Sobolev solution of
$(\star)$ on $J$** when

1. $u\in L^\infty(J;H^s)\cap C^0(J;H^{s-1})$ and the distributional time
   derivative $\partial_tu$ lies in $L^\infty(J;H^{s-1})$;
2. $u$ takes values in $O$ using the continuous representatives from (c);
3. for almost every $t\in J$ the identity $(\star)$ holds in
   $L^2(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$, with coefficients evaluated using
   the continuous representative of $u(t)$. This condition requires each
   displayed product to define an $L^2$ class; it does not assert a global
   coefficient-composition bound depending only on $\|u(t)\|_{H^s}$.

**(f) Initial data.** For an integer $s\ge5$, **initial data for $(\star)$ at
time $0$** are a class $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ whose values
lie in a compact subset of $O$; a solution **has initial value $u_0$** when
$u(t)\to u_0$ in $H^{s-1}$ as $t\to0$ within $J$.

The definition introduces the system and its solution classes only; existence,
uniqueness, continuous dependence and smooth persistence are asserted and
proved in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]],
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] and
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-smooth-persistence]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$
([[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]]) and let $K\subseteq O$ be
compact, and let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with $K$ contained in the
interior of $K'$. Then for every $R\ge0$ there are a time $T>0$ and a constant
$C$ (depending on $A^\mu,B,K,K',s$ and on $R$) such that:

for every $u_0\in H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ taking values in $K$ with
$\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$ there is a Sobolev solution
$u:(-T,T)\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ of $(\star)$ with
$u(0)=u_0$ which is classical and satisfies
$$u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0((-T,T);H^{s-1}),\quad \partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{s-1}),$$
$$\sup_{|t|<T}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C(1+R),\qquad \sup_{|t|<T}\|\partial_tu(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C(1+R),$$
and whose values lie in $K'$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq O$ be compact and $R\ge0$.

**(a) Uniqueness.** Let $J\ni0$ be an open interval and let
$u,v:J\to H^s(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$ be classical solutions of
$(\star)$ in the sense of clause (d) of
[[def-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-system]], both taking values in $K$ and
satisfying $\sup_{t\in J}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$, $\sup_{t\in J}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}\le R$.
If $u(0)=v(0)$, then $u=v$ on $J$.

**(b) Continuous dependence.** Let $K'\subseteq O$ be compact with
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'$ and let $T>0$ be a time for which the existence
theorem [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] produces solutions
from every datum with values in $K$ and norm at most $R$, with values in $K'$
and the bounds $C(1+R)$ of that theorem. Then for all such data $u_0,v_0$ with
solutions $u,v$
$$\|u(t)-v(t)\|_{H^{s-1}}\le C'\,e^{C'|t|}\,\|u_0-v_0\|_{H^{s-1}}\qquad(|t|<T),$$
with $C'=C'(A^\mu,B,K,K',R,s)$, the fixed compact coefficient time slab containing $[-T,T]$ being included in the coefficient data.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the data class $\mathcal S(K,R)$. Let $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^3_{2\pi};\mathbb R^m)$
take values in $K$ and satisfy $\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le R$. Then the solution $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^s)\cap C^0H^{s-1}$
of that theorem with $u(0)=u_0$ satisfies $u\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^q)$ and
$\partial_tu\in L^\infty((-T,T);H^{q-1})$ for every integer $q\ge s$, with bounds
depending only on $q$, $T$, $R$, the coefficient family, $K'$ and the $H^j$ bounds
of $u_0$ for $j\le q$; consequently $u\in C^\infty((-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi})$
and solves $(\star)$ classically.

derivations.claim: Apply [F3] to the state class and coefficient family in [F1]–[F2]. Its hypotheses match term by term: the unknown has $m$ real components on the specified $2\pi$-periodic torus, the coefficients are smooth on the same open state domain, $A^\mu$ are symmetric, $A^0$ is positive definite, the data range in compact $K\Subset K'$, and the integer regularity is $s\ge5$. It gives the common interval, value range, solution regularity and bounds.

For any two solutions in the stated bounded class with equal initial data, [F4] applies on the common interval and gives equality; its continuous-dependence estimate is exactly the claimed $H^{s-1}$ statement.
When the initial state is smooth, [F5] applies to the same solution from 1.1 and preserves smoothness on that same interval. No new interval or coupled Einstein-Maxwell conclusion is inferred.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

These are parameters of the mathematical system. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A Cauchy hypersurface is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$, future unit normal $n$, and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)=\tfrac12(\mathcal L_nh)(X,Y)$, using the convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. The Cauchy data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open set with smooth observer congruence $n$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$, and let $c>0$ be the coordinate conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Define covectors

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $c$ is the positive coordinate-conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with SI unit $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ in its length-coordinate convention. The names electric and magnetic distinguish these two covectors; for arbitrary mathematical $F$ no physical field unit or measurement is assigned.

For each $p\in U$, define the **rest covector space** by

$$\mathcal R^*_{n,p}:=\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n_p)=0\}.$$

The musical isomorphism $\flat_p$ maps the vector rest space $n_p^\perp$ onto $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$: $\alpha\in\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ iff $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,n_p)=\alpha(n_p)=0$. Moreover, $g_p^{-1}(v^\flat,w^\flat)=g_p(v,w)$, so the restriction of $g_p^{-1}$ to $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ is positive definite by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The covectors $E_p$ and $B_p$ annihilate $n_p$; define $\langle E,B\rangle_n(p):=g_p^{-1}(E_p,B_p)$. Then

$$F=n^\flat\wedge E/c+\star_g(n^\flat\wedge B),$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2\bigl(\langle B,B\rangle_n-\langle E,E\rangle_n/c^2\bigr),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2}{c}\langle E,B\rangle_n\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Equivalently, in any positively oriented future tetrad with $E_0=n$, and with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ in its oriented spatial triad, the components satisfy $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. These are pointwise mathematical decompositions of an arbitrary two-form; no Maxwell equation or physical observation is assumed.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$ and curvature $R$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). For a smooth vector field
$Z$ let $A$ be the smooth $(1,1)$-tensor field $A^a{}_b:=\nabla_bZ^a$ and
let $B:=\nabla A$ be its covariant derivative, $B^a{}_{bc}:=\nabla_bA^a{}_c$
([[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]] for the
extension of $\nabla$ to tensor fields).

**(a)** For all smooth vector fields $Z$ and all indices,
$$B^a{}_{bc}-B^a{}_{cb}=R^a{}_{dbc}Z^d .$$

**(b)** Contracting the first index with the second lower index,
$$B^a{}_{ab}-B^a{}_{ba}=\operatorname{Ric}_{bd}Z^d .$$

**(c)** For all smooth vector fields $V,Z$,
$$V^c\nabla_c(\nabla_aZ^a)=\nabla_a\bigl(V^c\nabla_cZ^a\bigr) -(\nabla_aV^c)(\nabla_cZ^a)-\operatorname{Ric}_{cd}V^cZ^d ,$$
where $\nabla_aW^a$ denotes the divergence of a vector field and
$\nabla_a(V^c\nabla_cZ^a)$ is the divergence of the vector field
$W^a:=V^c\nabla_cZ^a$.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

These are parameters of the mathematical system. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A Cauchy hypersurface is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$, future unit normal $n$, and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)=\tfrac12(\mathcal L_nh)(X,Y)$, using the convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. The Cauchy data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $s\ge5$ be an integer, let $A^\mu,B$ be a periodic symmetric
hyperbolic coefficient family on the open set $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, let
$K\subseteq\operatorname{int}K'\subseteq O$ be compact, let $R\ge0$, and let
$T>0$ and $C$ be as in [[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-existence]] for
the class $\mathcal S(K,R)$; for every datum $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ let $u$ be
the solution produced there on $(-T,T)$ with values in $K'$. Then:

**(a) [local existence]** For every $u_0\in\mathcal S(K,R)$ and every
$x_0\in\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ the solution $u$ is $C^1$ on a neighborhood of
$(0,x_0)$ in $(-T,T)\times\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$ and solves $(\star)$ pointwise
there.

**(b) [finite speed / independence of the extension]** Use the flat torus distance
$$d(q(x),q(y)):=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}|x-y+2\pi k|.$$
In any time-independent spatial chart $y$ with a local Euclidean lift $x(y)$ of $q$, put $h_{ij}(y)=\sum_a(\partial_i x^a)(\partial_j x^a)$; this is independent of the lift, since lifts differ by constant lattice translations, and write $h^{ij}$ for its inverse. A unit spatial covector in this clause means $\xi_i\,dy^i$ with $h^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j=1$. Let $\lambda_0>0$ be
determined by the coefficient bounds on a compact set containing the values of
the solutions in the following sense: for a truncated cone
$$D:=\{(t,x):0\le t\le t_0,\ d(x,x_0)\le\lambda(t_0-t)\}$$
with $0<t_0<T$, $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, lying in a single such spatial chart of $\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$
in which the coordinate representation of $A^\mu$ satisfies
$\lambda\,A^0+\xi_iA^i\ge0$ for every flat-metric unit covector $\xi$ at that point (such a $\lambda_0$ exists on compact coefficient sets by the norm-domination argument of clause (a) of [[lem-gr-finite-speed-independence-of-extension]], using the flat dual norm),
let $u,v$ be solutions of two periodic symmetric hyperbolic systems whose
coefficient functions agree on a neighborhood of $D$ in the independent variables and on one common open state set containing both solution ranges, with
$u(0,\cdot)=v(0,\cdot)$ on the ball $\{d(x,x_0)\le\lambda t_0\}$. Then
$u=v$ on $D$.

**(c) [local uniqueness and stability]** If two classical solutions of the same
system on a common interval have values in $K$, $H^s$ norms at most $R$ and the
same initial value, they coincide; and the continuous-dependence estimate of
[[thm-gr-periodic-symmetric-hyperbolic-uniqueness-stability]] clause (b) holds
for the solutions of clause (a).

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be the Lorentzian geometry and use the curvature convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Let $A_a$ be a smooth one-form, $A^a:=g^{ab}A_b$, and $F:=dA$, so $F_{ab}=\nabla_aA_b-\nabla_bA_a$ by torsion-freeness. Define $\Box_gA_b:=\nabla^a\nabla_aA_b$ and $\operatorname{div}A:=\nabla_aA^a$. Then

$$\nabla^aF_{ab}=\Box_gA_b-\nabla_b(\operatorname{div}A)-\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}A^c.$$

Consequently, if $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$, the Lorenz condition $\operatorname{div}A=0$ makes the potential equation

$$\Box_gA_b-\operatorname{Ric}_{bc}A^c=-\mu_0J_b.$$

The curvature term is part of the identity; this is not an uncoupled collection of scalar metric wave equations. The statement is local in the sense that it assumes a potential $A$ is already defined on the open set under consideration; it does not assert a global potential for every closed $F$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a
spacelike embedded hypersurface in the sense of
[[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (a), so that
$\Sigma$ is an embedded three-dimensional submanifold
([[def-embedded-submanifold-and-slice-chart]]) and the restriction of $g_p$
to $T_p\Sigma$ is positive definite for every $p\in\Sigma$
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). In the notation of
[[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] clause (a), whose claims
this lemma establishes:

**(a) The future unit normal.** For every $p\in\Sigma$ the orthogonal
complement $T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is one-dimensional, nondegenerate for $g_p$,
and negative definite: every nonzero $u\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ is timelike,
$g_p(u,u)<0$. Hence there is exactly one $n_p\in T_p\Sigma^{\perp}$ with
$g_p(n_p,n_p)=-1$ and $g_p(n_p,N_p)<0$.

**(b) Smoothness along the hypersurface.** The assignment $p\mapsto n_p$ is
smooth along $\Sigma$: for every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open neighborhood
$O$ of $p$ in $M$ and a smooth vector field $\tilde n$ on $O$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]) with
$\tilde n|_{\Sigma\cap O}=n|_{\Sigma\cap O}$, and for any two such local
extensions the covariant derivative at a point of $\Sigma$ in a direction
tangent to $\Sigma$ agrees. Thus for $V\in T_p\Sigma$ the vector
$\nabla_Vn\in T_pM$ is well defined as $\nabla_{\tilde X}\tilde n|_p$ for any
smooth extensions $\tilde n$ of $n$ and $\tilde X$ of a tangent field with
$\tilde X_p=V$ ([[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).

**(c) The induced metric and second fundamental form.** The **induced
metric** $h_p(V,W):=g_p(V,W)$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and
$$K_p(V,W):=g_p(\nabla_Vn,W)\qquad(V,W\in T_p\Sigma)$$
(the **second fundamental form**) defines a smooth symmetric covariant
$2$-tensor field $K$ on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) with
$$K_p(V,W)=-g_p(\nabla_VW,n_p),$$
where $\nabla_VW$ is the ambient covariant derivative at $p$ of any smooth
extension of a tangent field with value $W$ at $p$, in the direction of any
extension with value $V$ at $p$.

**(d) The shape operator.** The endomorphism $S_p:T_p\Sigma\to T_p\Sigma$
defined by $h_p(S_pV,W)=K_p(V,W)$ for all $W\in T_p\Sigma$ is well defined,
linear and self-adjoint for the positive definite form $h_p$, and the
Weingarten relation $\nabla_Vn=S_pV$ holds for every $V\in T_p\Sigma$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; its
Christoffel symbols are the smooth chart functions of
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]. Recall that a **geodesic**
is a curve with $D_t\gamma'=0$ in its parameter
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]]).

**(a) Local existence, uniqueness and maximality.** For every $(p,v)\in TM$
there is a unique maximal geodesic $\gamma_{p,v}:I_{p,v}\to M$ with
$\gamma_{p,v}(0)=p$ and $\gamma_{p,v}'(0)=v$; its domain $I_{p,v}$ is an open
interval containing $0$ and is not asserted to be all of $\mathbb R$.

**(b) Smooth dependence.** The set
$\mathcal G:=\{(t,p,v):t\in I_{p,v}\}\subseteq\mathbb R\times TM$ is open, and
the evaluation map $(t,p,v)\mapsto\gamma_{p,v}(t)$ is smooth on $\mathcal G$.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s\in\mathbb R$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$,
$t\in I_{p,sv}$ if and only if $st\in I_{p,v}$, and then
$\gamma_{p,sv}(t)=\gamma_{p,v}(st)$.

**(d) The exponential map.** Define $\mathcal E_p:=\{v\in T_pM:1\in I_{p,v}\}$
and $\exp_p:\mathcal E_p\to M$, $\exp_p(v):=\gamma_{p,v}(1)$, and let
$\psi_p:T_pM\to\mathbb R^4$ be the coordinate isomorphism of a basis
$e_0,\dots,e_3$ of $T_pM$. Then $\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about
$0$ (if $v\in\mathcal E_p$ and $0\le s\le1$, then $sv\in\mathcal E_p$),
$\exp_p$ is smooth, $\exp_p(0)=p$, and, under the canonical identification
$T_0(T_pM)\cong T_pM$ induced by the chart $\psi_p$ on $T_pM$,
$$d(\exp_p)_0=\operatorname{id}_{T_pM}.$$
Consequently there is a star-shaped open neighborhood $W_p\subseteq\mathcal E_p$
of $0$ such that $\exp_p|_{W_p}$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of
$M$.

Let $F:M\to N$ be a smooth map and let $p\in M$. If $dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N$ is
an isomorphism, then there are open neighbourhoods $U$ of $p$ and $V$ of
$F(p)$ such that $F|_U:U\to V$ is a diffeomorphism.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection; its existence and uniqueness are
supplied by [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Fix
$c>0$. All intervals $I,J$ below have nonempty interior. For a
smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ write $D_t$ for the covariant derivative along
$\gamma$ of [[def-covariant-derivative-along-a-curve]] with respect to
$\nabla$ (equivalently, the pullback of the Levi–Civita connection).

1. **Metric pairing.** For smooth sections $V,W$ of the pullback bundle
   $\gamma^*TM$,
   $$\frac{d}{dt}\,g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),W(t)\bigr)=g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(D_tV(t),W(t)\bigr)+g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(V(t),D_tW(t)\bigr).$$
   In particular, if $D_tV=D_tW=0$ on $I$, then $g(V,W)$ is constant on $I$.

2. **Parallel transport.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise smooth curve
   with $a<b$.
   For every $v\in T_{\gamma(a)}M$ there is exactly one continuous piecewise
   smooth section $V$ of $\gamma^*TM$ with $D_tV=0$ on each smooth piece and
   $V(a)=v$; the parallel-transport map
   $P_\gamma:T_{\gamma(a)}M\to T_{\gamma(b)}M$, $v\mapsto V(b)$, is linear,
   bijective, and satisfies
   $g_{\gamma(b)}(P_\gamma v,P_\gamma w)=g_{\gamma(a)}(v,w)$ for all $v,w$.
   For $a=b$, the unique section is its prescribed fibre vector and
   $P_\gamma$ is the identity; no $D_t$ condition is imposed on a singleton.

3. **Geodesic speed and proper time.** Along a geodesic
   $\gamma:I\to M$ ([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) the function
   $t\mapsto g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))$ is constant. If $\gamma$
   is nonconstant, its tangent is nowhere zero and its causal character
   (timelike, null or spacelike) is constant; a constant geodesic has zero
   tangent and is assigned none of those causal characters. If $\gamma$ is a
   **future-directed timelike geodesic** and
   $g(\gamma',\gamma')=-\lambda^2$ with $\lambda>0$, then for
   $t_0<t_1$ its proper-time increment over $[t_0,t_1]$ is
   $\lambda(t_1-t_0)/c$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]), so proper time is an
   affine parameter. In this parameter its four-velocity is
   $U=(c/\lambda)\gamma'$ and is parallel: $D_\tau U=0$. Proper time is not
   assigned to a past-directed curve by that definition; reversing the
   parameter gives a future-directed timelike geodesic with the same
   (positive) proper-time magnitude. A nonconstant null geodesic has null
   tangent and admits no proper-time parametrization.

4. **Affine reparametrizations.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a geodesic whose
   tangent is nowhere zero, and let $h:J\to I$ be a $C^2$ diffeomorphism onto
   its open image with $h'\neq0$. Then $\gamma\circ h$ is a geodesic if and
   only if $h(s)=as+b$ with constants $a\neq0$, $b$; in that case $a$ is the
   constant $h'$, and every affine parameter of this nonconstant geodesic
   arises in this way from a fixed one. If $\gamma$ is constant, then
   $\gamma\circ h$ is constant and hence geodesic for every such $h$; no
   affine restriction on $h$ follows.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable four-manifold without boundary, with smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and smooth time-orientation field $N$, as in [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]. Supply an independent orientation $o$ of $M$ in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. The metric and time orientation do not select $o$. Write $\mathrm{vol}_g$ for the oriented metric volume form of [[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]; in any positively oriented chart it has components $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$.

A smooth real $k$-form is a smooth section of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, and its space is denoted $\Omega^k(M)$, as in [[def-smooth-differential-k-form]]. In this page, $F\in\Omega^2(M)$ means an arbitrary smooth real two-form. No equation such as $dF=0$, no global potential, and no physical field law is included in this definition.

An **observer at $p\in M$** is a vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $g_p(n,N_p)<0$; its **rest space** is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. A smooth **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth vector field whose value at every point is an observer. Its observer curves are the maximal integral curves, and a chart is adapted to it when its three spatial coordinate functions are constant along those curves, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]. Such a congruence need not be hypersurface-orthogonal.

A **local frame field** on $U$ is an ordered smooth basis field of $TM|_U$. A **coordinate frame** is the basis of coordinate vector fields supplied by a chart. A **tetrad field** is a local frame $(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3)$ with $g(E_A,E_B)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)_{AB}$; it is future-directed when $E_0$ is future-directed, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. These are distinct objects: an observer congruence is a vector field, an adapted chart is a coordinate chart, and a tetrad is a basis field. A tetrad field is not presumed to be a coordinate frame. For every observer congruence $n$, each point has a neighborhood carrying an $n$-adapted tetrad; this is a local assertion only.

A **worldline** on this Lorentzian manifold means a $C^1$ or piecewise-$C^1$ regular curve with future-timelike tangent and specified interval domain, as defined precisely in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. Its parameter is arbitrary; the proper-time and four-velocity constructions of that definition apply under their stated hypotheses. A worldline is a mathematical curve here and does not assert the existence or motion of a physical body.

For coordinate bookkeeping only, when a chart is chosen with all four coordinate values assigned the metre, write $x^0=ct$, where $t$ is assigned seconds and $c>0$ is the corresponding scale in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$. Then $g_{ab}$ is recorded as dimensionless. This is a unit convention on a chart, not a claim that the chart is inertial, orthonormal, global, or physically realized; $c$ in this mathematical convention has no asserted measured value.

Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]]. In a length-coordinate chart, the displayed Christoffel formula differentiates dimensionless metric components once, so $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ is recorded in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. The curvature coordinate formula contains one derivative of $\Gamma$ or a product of two $\Gamma$ components, so $R^a{}_{bcd}$ and its Ricci and scalar contractions are recorded in $\mathrm m^{-2}$. These component assignments apply only in length-coordinate charts; other coordinate units transform by their Jacobians.

Let $a<b$ and $c<d$. Suppose $g,h:[a,b]\times[c,d]\to\mathbb R$ are continuous and, for every fixed $t\in[c,d]$, the function $x\mapsto g(x,t)$ is differentiable on $(a,b)$ with derivative $h(x,t)$. Define

$$G(x):=\int_c^d g(x,t)\,dt.$$

Then $G$ is differentiable on $[a,b]$ as a function on that interval and

$$G'(x)=\int_c^d h(x,t)\,dt\qquad(x\in[a,b]).$$

At $a$ and $b$ the derivative is relative and one-sided. The derivative hypothesis is imposed only for interior parameter values; continuity of $h$ supplies its endpoint values.

The coordinate identity $dF=0$ in [F1] gives $\partial_kF_{ba}-\partial_aF_{bk}=\partial_bF_{ka}$. The integrand is therefore $\frac{d}{dt}(t^2F_{ka}(tx))$, whose integral is $F_{ka}(x)$ because the lower endpoint is zero. Thus $dA=F$. On every compact coordinate rectangle around a point of $U$, the integrand and all its coordinate derivatives are continuous on the product with $[0,1]$; apply [F8] one derivative at a time to prove smoothness of $A$.

For a smooth scalar $\chi$, [F1] gives $d(A+d\chi)=dA+d^2\chi=dA$, and metric compatibility in [F7] gives $
abla^a(A_a+
abla_a\chi)=

abla^aA_a$ with zero initial value and zero initial normal derivative on a smaller spacelike patch.

Fix $p\in S$. By [F4] the future unit normal $n_y$ varies smoothly in a slice neighborhood. By [F5] the geodesic flow $(t,y,v)\mapsto\gamma_{y,v}(t)$ is smooth near $(0,p,n_p)$, so $\Phi(t,y):=\gamma_{y,n_y}(t)$ is smooth. At $(0,p)$ its differential sends the time direction to $n_p$ and slice tangent vectors to themselves; these span $T_pM$, so [F5] makes $\Phi$ a coordinate chart after shrinking. Put $T=\partial_0$ and $J_i=\partial_i$. The geodesic equation gives $
abla_TT=0$ and [F6] gives $g(T,T)=-1$. Since $[T,J_i]=0$, torsion-freeness in [F7] gives $
abla_TJ_i=
abla_{J_i}T$, so $\partial_0g(T,J_i)=g(
abla_TT,J_i)+g(T,
abla_TJ_i)=	frac12J_i(g(T,T))=0$. At $t=0$, $g(T,J_i)=g(n,J_i)=0$ by [F4]; hence $g_{0i}=0$ and $g_{00}=-1$ throughout the smaller chart. By continuity the spatial metric stays positive on a smaller relatively compact chart, so $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite.

Write $f=-\nabla^aA_a$, $p_0=\partial_0\chi$, and $q_i=\partial_i\chi$. The wave equation, together with $\partial_0\chi=p_0$ and $\partial_0q_i=\partial_ip_0$, is equivalent to $\partial_0\chi-p_0=0$, $-g^{00}\partial_0p_0-2g^{0k}\partial_kp_0-g^{ij}\partial_iq_j+L(p_0,q)=-f$, and $g^{ij}(\partial_0q_j-\partial_jp_0)=0$, where $L$ is the smooth first-order lower-order expression from expanding $\Box_g\chi$. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

These are parameters of the mathematical system. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A Cauchy hypersurface is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$, future unit normal $n$, and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)=\tfrac12(\mathcal L_nh)(X,Y)$, using the convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. The Cauchy data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ be the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=\operatorname{tr}_hK$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, take $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, integer $s\ge5$, $h\in H^{s+1}$, $K,e,b\in H^s$, and assume the continuous representative of $h$ has a uniform positive lower eigenvalue bound. The displayed constraint expressions then have continuous representatives: their weak-derivative orders are at most two for $h$ and one for $K,e,b$, and the embedding, algebra and smooth-composition suppliers [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-embedding]], [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]], and [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] apply. In SI coordinates $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, while $e,b$ have units tesla; the coefficients $\kappa/\mu_0$ give the displayed terms matching units.

Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on a smooth oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with the connection, Hodge star, and tensor $Q_{ab}=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\tfrac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. For a smooth vector field $J$, suppose

$$dF=0,\qquad \nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b.$$

Then $Q_{ab}$ is symmetric and trace-free, and the SI-normalized stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}$ satisfies

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=-F_{bc}J^c.$$

In the source-free case $J=0$, $\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, put $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$, $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$, and $(e\times b)_i:=\epsilon_{ijk}e_jb_k$. Then

$$T^{\rm EM}(n,n)=\frac{|e|^2+|b|^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{\rm EM}(n,\mathfrak e_i)=-\frac{(e\times b)_i}{\mu_0}.$$

These are pointwise tensor identities. In the SI interpretation $e=E/c$ and $b=B$ have units tesla; no measurement or physical applicability claim is included.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $U\subseteq M$ be an open set with smooth observer congruence $n$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form on $U$, and let $c>0$ be the coordinate conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Define covectors

$$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b,\qquad B_a:=-({\star_gF})_{ab}n^b.$$

Here $c$ is the positive coordinate-conversion parameter of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]], with SI unit $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ in its length-coordinate convention. The names electric and magnetic distinguish these two covectors; for arbitrary mathematical $F$ no physical field unit or measurement is assigned.

For each $p\in U$, define the **rest covector space** by

$$\mathcal R^*_{n,p}:=\{\alpha\in T_p^*M:\alpha(n_p)=0\}.$$

The musical isomorphism $\flat_p$ maps the vector rest space $n_p^\perp$ onto $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$: $\alpha\in\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ iff $g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,n_p)=\alpha(n_p)=0$. Moreover, $g_p^{-1}(v^\flat,w^\flat)=g_p(v,w)$, so the restriction of $g_p^{-1}$ to $\mathcal R^*_{n,p}$ is positive definite by [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]. The covectors $E_p$ and $B_p$ annihilate $n_p$; define $\langle E,B\rangle_n(p):=g_p^{-1}(E_p,B_p)$. Then

$$F=n^\flat\wedge E/c+\star_g(n^\flat\wedge B),$$

$$F_{ab}F^{ab}=2\bigl(\langle B,B\rangle_n-\langle E,E\rangle_n/c^2\bigr),\qquad F\wedge F=-\frac{2}{c}\langle E,B\rangle_n\,\mathrm{vol}_g.$$

Equivalently, in any positively oriented future tetrad with $E_0=n$, and with $\epsilon_{123}=+1$ in its oriented spatial triad, the components satisfy $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. These are pointwise mathematical decompositions of an arbitrary two-form; no Maxwell equation or physical observation is assumed.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ have the oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian structure and volume form of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. On decomposable $k$-covectors define the induced exterior pairing by

$$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det\bigl(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j)\bigr),$$

and extend it bilinearly. For $0\le k\le4$, its coordinate expression is the pointwise exterior metric on $k$-covectors

$$\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g:=\frac1{k!}\alpha_{a_1\cdots a_k}\beta^{a_1\cdots a_k},$$

where indices are raised by $g^{-1}$. There is a unique smooth bundle map $\star_g:\Omega^k(M)\to\Omega^{4-k}(M)$ characterized by

$$\alpha\wedge\star_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$$

at every point. In a positively oriented $g$-orthonormal coframe $(e^0,e^1,e^2,e^3)$, put $\epsilon_0=-1$ and $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=\epsilon_3=1$. For an increasing index set $I\subseteq\{0,1,2,3\}$, let $I^c$ be its increasing complement, let $s(I,I^c)$ be the sign of the permutation $(I,I^c)$ to $(0,1,2,3)$, and set $\epsilon_I:=\prod_{i\in I}\epsilon_i$. Then

$$\star_g e^I=\epsilon_I s(I,I^c)e^{I^c}.$$

Consequently, on $k$-forms,

$$\star_g^2=(-1)^{k(4-k)+1}\operatorname{id}.$$

In particular $\star_g^2=-\operatorname{id}$ on two-forms. For a two-form $F$, the component formula in a positively oriented chart is

$$({\star_gF})_{ab}=\frac12(\mathrm{vol}_g)_{abcd}F^{cd}.$$

The exterior derivative in [[def-exterior-derivative-by-the-invariant-vector-field-formula]] has the local coordinate formula of [[thm-local-coordinate-formula-for-the-exterior-derivative]], satisfies $d^2=0$, and obeys the graded product rule of [[thm-the-exterior-derivative-is-a-graded-derivation]].

derivations.claim: In a positively oriented local orthonormal tetrad $(n,\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$, [F4] gives $i^*F=\star_h b^\flat$ and $i^*(\star_gF)=\star_h e^\flat$. Pullback commutes with exterior differentiation, so [A1] implies $d_\Sigma(\star_hb^\flat)=0$ and $d_\Sigma(\star_he^\flat)=0$. In oriented coordinates, $\operatorname{vol}_h=\sqrt{\det h}\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and $\star_hv^\flat=\iota_v\operatorname{vol}_h$; differentiating gives $d_\Sigma(\iota_v\operatorname{vol}_h)=\partial_i(\sqrt{\det h}\,v^i)\,dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3=(D_iv^i)\operatorname{vol}_h$, since $\Gamma^i{}_{ik}=\partial_k\log\sqrt{\det h}$. Therefore $D_ib^i=0$ and $D_ie^i=0$.

Apply [F3] to the existing solution in [A1]. The normal-normal projection of $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T^{\rm EM}$ gives $\tfrac12(R(h)+\tau^2-|K|^2)-\Lambda=\kappa T^{\rm EM}(n,n)$ because $g(n,n)=-1$. Substitute [F2] and multiply by $2$ to obtain the Hamiltonian constraint.

For any tangent $V$, the normal-tangential projection gives $G(n,V)=\kappa T^{\rm EM}(n,V)$ because $g(n,V)=0$. Substitute [F2]–[F3] to get $(D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau)V^i=-(\kappa/\mu_0)h(e\times_hb,V)$. Since this holds for every tangent $V$, the two covectors are equal, proving the momentum constraint.

The Maxwell divergence identities from 1.1 and the Einstein normal projections from 1.2–1.3 are exactly the four equations defining constrained data in [F1]. Thus the induced tuple satisfies that definition.

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]].
